narrative.northStar: Call Numbers, embellished in Rubric & Lapis
narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "Call Numbers, embellished in Rubric & Lapis"**

Glose is a library desk, not a file tree. Every Source wears a call number (three letters of the author's family name and the first-publication year, typed on a white label) that leads back to the page. The app is embellished the way old books are: at the edges, never in the text. A lapis rail holds the Sections like a bound spine; panels are white leaves on a near-white ground, each opened by a decorated initial and a small red pen flourish set in a hairline rule.

The mode is Operate. Density is calm and working: lapis marks the next step, panels that say what to do next when empty, data set plainly in Public Sans with tabular numerals. Ornament (Cinzel initials, the flourish, gilt bands, the gold current marker) lives on headings and chrome. Data, Note text and controls stay plain. The world refuses the category's file-tree-plus-editor arrangement in neutral grey, and it refuses dashboards and gamification.

Every string comes from the English and Danish catalogs (`i18n/en.ts`, `i18n/da.ts`; the lint rule `glose/no-untranslated-ui-text` enforces this), and every layout takes the longer Danish compounds without clipping.

AI text carries rubric marks at its edge (a red pilcrow, a gloss and a rule) while the text itself stays ink; see the AI Text component in DESIGN.md.
keyCharacteristics: Lapis rail (96px) of large Section icons with labels under them; gold marks the current one.
White panels with hairline borders; each heading opens with a rubric or lapis Cinzel initial, alternating down a column, above a hairline with a rubric pen flourish in its middle.
Call numbers as typed white spine labels in Courier Prime with a 1px ink border.
Flat surfaces; depth comes from hairlines and the ground/paper step, not shadows.
Red is a signal with fixed jobs, never a decoration of data.
A focus screen (Review) drops the rail and the page header: one Paper leaf on Ground.

rules.name: The Rubric Rule
rules.body: Rubric red marks the decorated initials, the pen flourish and AI text. When red marks an error or missing data, it always comes with a warning icon and words; red alone never carries a meaning.

rules.name: The Gilt Marker Rule
rules.body: Gold says "here": the current Section, the current step, a spine's bands, focus on lapis. It is never used for text on paper or for decoration elsewhere.

rules.name: The One Field Rule
rules.body: Lapis is the only large color field (rail, spine, the primary button). Panels and the page stay paper and ground.

rules.name: The One Initial Rule
rules.body: Cinzel Decorative appears only as the first letter of a panel heading, the setup title or the Review bar title, through `::first-letter`, so the heading text stays whole for screen readers. Never on data, buttons or body.

rules.name: The Typed Label Rule
rules.body: Courier Prime is for call numbers and step numbers only.

rules.name: The Danish Length Rule
rules.body: No layout depends on the length of English text. Heads, rows and button rows wrap; rail labels hyphenate and break anywhere; nothing truncates a label. Check every new screen in Danish.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Panels separate by a 1px Hairline and a white leaf on Ground. Don't add resting shadows.

dos: Do put ornament (initials, flourish, gilt) on headings and chrome only, and the flourish in the hairline rule between a Review question and its answer.
Do alternate panel initials rubric and lapis down each column.
Do pair every red error or missing-data signal with a warning icon and words.
Do use Gilt only to mark the current place (Section, step) and focus on lapis.
Do give every Source its call number label wherever it is listed.
Do take every string from the EN/DA catalogs and check the layout in Danish.
Do keep Lapis buttons for the next step forward (Add Source, Continue, Start); other actions are ink-outlined secondary.
Do give every button on a focus screen that a key presses a key cap, and name the key in `aria-keyshortcuts`.
Do use tabular numerals for counts, years and call numbers.
donts: Don't decorate data, Note text, inputs or buttons (no initials, flourishes or gilt there).
Don't use red alone to mean anything; color never carries a message by itself.
Don't add resting shadows or new fields of color beyond the lapis rail, spine and primary.
Don't use Cinzel Decorative beyond a single heading initial, or Courier Prime beyond call and step numbers.
Don't fix widths to English text, truncate labels, or block wrapping.
Don't build a file-tree-plus-editor arrangement in neutral grey, a busy dashboard, or gamification.
